newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures close higher.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures close higher.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures ended higher, but June Standard & Poor's 500s forfeited their record gains due to what some traders said was a disappointing close in the U.S. bond market.
"People were disappointed with the bond close," one S&P futures trader said. "We had such a good producer price number this morning and yet you didn't get much followthrough."

U.S. bond futures ended below session peaks even though the U.S. April producer price index fell 0.6 percent, lessening market expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise U.S. interest rates at its policy meeting on Tuesday.

U.S. traders are awaiting the U.S. April consumer price index at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Thursday. CPI is seen rising 0.1 percent and core CPI is forecast to gain 0.2 percent, unchanged from March's overall and core rates.

"Some reports show strong economic growth, others weak growth, so it's really hard to determine what the market is expecting from the Fed next week," another trader said. "It's making people especially nervous."
Comments by former Federal Reserve chairman Paul Volcker added to the nervous tone. In a television interview, Volcker said the danger of faster inflation was drawing closer.

The market's nervousness was reflected in June S&Ps' 10.80-point intraday range. The contract often whipped 2.00 points in either direction for no apparent reason, and led to arbitrage buy and sell programs, they said.
"We got as cheap as 1.95 in premium and as rich as 9.00," one trader said.

The contract only needed to rise 4.30 points above cash to touch off arbitrage buy programs and trade 2.70 points over cash to hit arbitrage sell programs, traders said. Fair value remained at about 3.10 points to cash.
One floor trader said May options expiration on Friday was also making trade choppy.
"By Wednesday you see a lot of dealers trying to square positions and that creates volatility," one floor source said.
However, June's last downside price move for the day occurred from long liquidation and put the contract into negative territory. June fell to 835.50, below support at 836.00 to 836.40.
"People are so afraid to the buy the highs to begin with," another pit trader said. "So when the market shows any sign of falling back, people immediately liquidate their positions."
He said June S&Ps should hold losses at the 824.00 level, and agreed with the majority of traders that the contract is more likely to test the upside rather than downside.
Within the first 10 minutes of pit trade, June S&Ps set an all-time high of 846.30. The contract initially rallied to the seven-point opening limit due to the PPI data.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were up 2.70 points at 839.95, KCBT Value Lines were up 2.95 at 736.25, NYSE Composites were up 1.80 at 437.65, Nikkeis were 100 higher at 20,315, Russell 2000s were up 1.50 at 367.75, Midcap 400s were up 1.75 at 271.45 and Nasdaq 100s lost 2.50 at 916.25.
